newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall 1.49 pct on selling.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall 1.49 pct on selling.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended their losses as selling accelerated on Wednesday afternoon amid unconfirmed market rumours that international credit agencies may downgrade Turkey's debt rating soon, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 1,388.32 points, or 1.49 percent lower at 91,828.79, bringing three-day losses to 2.73 percent since Friday's all-time high closing of 94,407.22. It bounced slightly from a low of 91,025 on late buys.
Trade volume dropped to 13.69 trillion lira from Tuesday's 14.36 trillion.
"The market was having a normal correction which was awaited, but credit rating rumours increased caution and sales in the market today," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.
"It will be more healthy if the index falls to the 90,000 mark before an expected year-end rise. A possible decision on Turkey's credit rating may not emerge for some days."
Standard & Poor's had put Turkey under creditwatch with negative implications and other Western agencies IBCA and Duff & Phelps had said they might downgrade Turkey's ratings in July.

The stock market has since been susceptible to rumours or press speculation which emerge every now and then on the issue. Treasury officials told Reuters a decision by S&P was expected by the end this month.
"Low volume shows that the falls may not continue. A recovery based on end-year profit prospects is possible," said Alp Tekince from Bumerang securities.
The index had leapt 2.89 percent last week after a 5.49 percent surge the previous week and hit nine record closes in the last two weeks.

Of the 231 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 154 to 31 and 46 were unchanged. The 85-share industrial index fell 1.52 percent to 96,329.46 and the 15-share financial index dropped 1.42 percent to 90,276.01.

Actives were led by steel rope producer Celik Halat, up 600 lira at 6,200, largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 12,500 and Ihlas Holding, down 750 lira at 14,750. Together, they made up 18.5 percent of the total turnover.
